thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING: High GPU queue + error spike observed in pool `ml-prod-2`. severity=P1. queue_length~=1800, ready_gpus=12, pending_jobs=420. Paging @oncall and @sre. https://ops.internal/incidents/2187654321

maria: I'm on it — starting with autoscaler + driver logs.

ashok: taking pager. moving to #eng-oncall-handovers. Maria, what's the current desired scale target and why didn't it happen automatically?

maria: autoscaler attempted scale up 12->20 but cloud returned 403 QuotaExceeded. Also seeing a spike of CUDA/Xid errors on several nodes (Xid 45), and nvml reports repeated OOMs. Multiple nodes are flapping.

kevin: can you paste the autoscaler/cloud output?

maria: ```
autoscaler: scaling request -> desired=20
cloud-api: error 403 QuotaExceeded: GPUs per region limit 20
driver-monitor: cuda/xid=45 count=68 since 10m
node-ctl: node-ml-05 flapping: kubelet restart loop
```

jess: quick options: (1) divert new/non-realtime jobs to backup pool `ml-prod-3`, (2) throttle ingress to ml-prod-2, (3) roll driver on flapping nodes. I'd start with 1+2 to stop queue growth.

ashok: agree. Maria — apply routing rule to send non-critical traffic to ml-prod-3. Kevin — reduce the rate limit on ml-prod-2.

kevin: doing the rate-limit patch now. dropping qps to 40 for ml-prod-2. patch command:
```
curl -X POST http://console/api/rate_limit -d '{"pool":"ml-prod-2","qps":40}'
```

maria: applying routing change to prefer ml-prod-3 for tags!=realtime:
```
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
data:
  route: "prefer:ml-prod-3 for tags!=realtime"
EOF
```

maria: routing applied. queue length flattening: 1800 -> 720 in ~6m. inbound QPS dropped ~45%. :thumbsup:

ashok: driver symptoms — repeated 'Xid 45' and oom-kill seen in dmesg. I'd like a rolling driver restart to reclaim GPUs on the worst nodes. Maria, schedule drain/restart for four nodes, one at a time.

maria: starting rolling restart on node-ml-05 -> node-ml-08. Steps: cordon/drain -> delete driver pods -> uncordon.
```
kubectl cordon node-ml-05
kubectl drain node-ml-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl delete pod -l app=driver -n gpu-ops --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-ml-05
kubectl uncordon node-ml-05
```

support-eng: CS note: customers C-3456 and C-4821 reported tail-latency spikes. CS is preparing outreach. ETA update to customers in ~15m.

ashok: good. Any progress on autoscaler quota?

maria: autoscaler would be happy to scale if quota permitted. I filed a provider ticket (CP-89274) requesting temporary quota increase — ETA ~30m. We need an interim burst strategy.

kevin: can we spin up a burst pool in another region with preemptible GPUs and attach to k8s?

maria: launching burst provisioning script to create ml-burst-1 (preemptible a100)
```
./provision_burst_pool.sh --region=us-west2 --count=6 --type=a100-preemptible
```

kevin: provisioning output: 4/6 instances ready, kube join successful for those 4. Attaching to cluster and labeling as pool=ml-burst-1.

maria: added nodes to pool, moved low-priority jobs to ml-burst-1. queue now dropping: ~420 -> ~60 pending. core latency improving.

support-eng: CS sent the P1 customer notification and offered degraded SLA credits. Customers acknowledged receipt and are tracking.

oncall-bot: Handoff: ashok -> kevin for the next 2 hours. Logging current mitigation steps and timeline to the incident tracker.

jess: post-incident action items (RCA):
- quota monitoring + pre-emptive requests for expected peak.
- autoscaler: better fallbacks when drivers fail (don't rely purely on scale up).
- investigate driver/kernel stability (Xid 45/OOM correlation).
- add pre-warm/burst automation.
Assignments: ashok -> cloud quota escalation + follow-up with provider, maria -> incident writeup + logs, kevin -> rate-limiter + routing automation, jess -> schedule RCA postmortem.

ashok: severity downgraded to P2, closing pager for now. Queue normalized and driver restarts reclaimed ~8 GPUs. Cloud quota ticket open (CP-89274).

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED for `ml-prod-2` — root cause summary: driver/runtime instability (OOM/Xid) caused effective GPU capacity loss while autoscaler attempts were blocked by cloud GPU quota limits. Follow-ups created: INC-2187654321-RCA.

maria: thanks team — I'll post a short timeline and attach logs to the tracker. we'll need FW/kernel val checks and a playbook for burst pools. :memo:

kevin: noted — will add automation to detect quota-blocked scale attempts and automatically provision burst pool next time.

jess: great work. will own the postmortem and invite infra, runtime, and platform owners.
